title: Interactive decision-tree microinteractions and diagnostic kit for error states
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design an interactive decision-tree style diagnostic asset kit for onboarding and quickstart docs that helps users understand and recover from common runtime failures: rate limits, request timeouts, and retry behavior. The kit should include: a) compact decision-tree illustrations for docs (printable + responsive), b) microinteraction specs for UI components (snackbars, retry buttons, cooldown timers), c) annotated product screenshots with layered callouts for Console and API errors, and d) a single-page trouble-shooting flow for embedded quickstarts that can be converted into HTML/CSS/JS by frontend. Focus is on low-friction recovery language, clear next-actions, and measurable telemetry hooks for engineering to implement UX instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Three distinct decision-tree diagrams covering rate limits, timeouts, and retryable errors in both full-size and compact variants
Microinteraction specs documented with timing, easing, and accessible motion-reduction alternatives
Annotated Console screenshots (error toast, route dashboard, per-token cost panel) with callout copy and developer-friendly remediation steps
Exportable asset package (SVGs, PNGs, Lottie JSON for one microinteraction) and a conversion-ready HTML snippet for embedding in quickstarts
Design review signoff from PM and Eng and a linked GitHub issue for implementation work
Usability sanity test with 3 internal engineers showing they can resolve a simulated rate-limit using the flow
assets_needed: SVG icon set for error states (throttle, clock, loop/retry)
Two annotated Console screenshots (route-level and token-level panels)
Copy deck with short remediation steps and microcopy variants
decisions: Use decision-tree metaphor rather than linear checklist to reduce cognitive load for multi-cause failures
Prioritize a single persistent CTA ("retry with backoff") plus contextual alternatives ("switch model" or "reduce batch size")
Provide a compact single-line explanation for each node (12-18 words) and a learn-more link for advanced guidance
Include an accessible reduced-motion microinteraction for users with prefers-reduced-motion enabled
Expose telemetry anchors in designs (error_code, request_id, suggestion_selected) so Eng can instrument SLO-aligned metrics
